source_reconciliation.source_order: The seed and TSV have distinct orders; a bijection preserves every occurrence.

products.description: The displayed 134-residue product contains the heme-binding domain and the C-terminal transmembrane segment at residues 109–131. The official mature chain is 2–134 after initiator methionine removal. Heme ligands are His44 and His68. Membrane-associated redox functions are principally assigned to this product, with experimental construct limits retained for individual sources.

The 98-residue product is independently reconstructed by VSP_001240 (Thr98Pro) and VSP_001241 (residues 99–134 absent). It lacks the membrane anchor. The historical erythrocyte sequence in PMID:4030743 has 97 residues after initiator methionine removal; that numbering is not a different 98-residue precursor sequence. The official record notes possible low-level expression through nonsense-mediated decay. It is not equated with arbitrary soluble constructs used in P450 assays.

The 124-residue product is independently reconstructed by VSP_045367, deleting canonical residues 86–95. It retains the heme-ligating residues and membrane-anchor sequence, but this structural compatibility does not establish equal partner specificity, abundance or catalytic support relative to product 1.

core_scope.human_direct_evidence: 22170710 human CYB5A/CYP17A1 coexpression enhances lyase, without directly measuring electron transfer or H44L heme loss.
core_scope.mechanistic_ortholog_evidence: 29888793 human CYP17A1 + rat reductase + rabbit b5 directly measures electron transfer; 27297105 and33656879 constrain redox versus substrate-dependent conformational interpretations.
core_scope.annotation_decision: One NEW GO:0009055 ISS assertion uses rabbit CYB5A P00169 mechanistic evidence with human functional corroboration. All 21 original source objects and omitted isoform fields are preserved. No human-b5 IDA, all-product equivalence or new BP is asserted.
core_scope.activation_term_considered: GO:0008047 requires direct interaction without covalent modification. CYP17A1 enhancement is described explicitly; a second core restating the same partner-support step was not added.

ortholog_inference.evidence: PMID:29888793 Methods and Results, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6369587/; actual rabbit-b5 kinetics, not direct human IDA or experimentally verified plasmid sequence.

ontology.name: actin binding
ontology.definition: Binding to monomeric or multimeric forms of actin, including actin filaments.

ontology.name: cytoplasm
ontology.definition: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

ontology.name: mitochondrial outer membrane
ontology.definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the mitochondrial envelope.

ontology.name: endoplasmic reticulum
ontology.definition: The irregular network of unit membranes, visible only by electron microscopy, that occurs in the cytoplasm of many eukaryotic cells. The membranes form a complex meshwork of tubular channels, which are often expanded into slitlike cavities called cisternae. The ER takes two forms, rough (or granular), with ribosomes adhering to the outer surface, and smooth (with no ribosomes attached).

ontology.name: endoplasmic reticulum membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the endoplasmic reticulum.

ontology.name: cytosol
ontology.definition: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.

ontology.name: cytoskeletal protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein component of a cytoskeleton (actin, microtubule, or intermediate filament cytoskeleton).

ontology.name: membrane
ontology.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

ontology.name: kinesin binding
ontology.definition: Interacting selectively and non-covalently and stoichiometrically with kinesin, a member of a superfamily of microtubule-based motor proteins that perform force-generating tasks such as organelle transport and chromosome segregation.

ontology.name: enzyme binding
ontology.definition: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

ontology.name: heme binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a heme, a compound composed of iron complexed in a porphyrin (tetrapyrrole) ring.

ontology.name: ubiquitin protein ligase binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a ubiquitin protein ligase enzyme, any of the E3 proteins.

ontology.name: ubiquitin-like protein ligase binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a ubiquitin-like protein ligase, such as ubiquitin-ligase.

ontology.name: enzyme activator activity
ontology.definition: A molecular function regulator that increases a catalytic activity.
ontology.comment: This term should only be used in cases when the regulator directly interacts with the enzyme, but does not result in a covalent modification.

ontology.name: electron transfer activity
ontology.definition: A molecular function representing the directed movement of electrons from one molecular entity to another, typically mediated by electron carriers or acceptors, resulting in the transfer of energy and/or the reduction-oxidation (redox) transformation of chemical species. This activity is fundamental to various biological processes, including cellular respiration and photosynthesis, as well as numerous enzymatic reactions involved in metabolic pathways.

primary_sources.title: Interactions of mammalian cytochrome P450, NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, and cytochrome b(5) enzymes.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract explicitly reports the four seeded P450 interactions and an immobilized purified-protein affinity assay. Exact b5 species/construct and full Methods remain unavailable; current literal pair absence is not a negative result.

primary_sources.title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
primary_sources.assessment: Identifier/title and human NK-like YTS membrane-proteomics context are verified from the complete abstract. The CYB5A target table/peptides remain unverified after two failed supplementary-table routes; no full-original or target-table read is claimed.

primary_sources.title: Different effects of Sec61α, Sec62 and Sec63 depletion on transport of polypeptides into the endoplasmic reticulum of mammalian cells.
primary_sources.assessment: The cache flag says full text but its body includes only Abstract/Introduction. Separate indexed original Results, Figure 2D/Table 1 discussion and protein-transport Methods were read. The cytb5-ops28 ER-insertion assay is explicit; exact construct species/sequence and figure pixels were not verified.

primary_sources.title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
primary_sources.assessment: Original author PDF selected Results and automated Y2H Methods were read; fifteen exact current records independently establish the five seeded human pairs and thirty participant ROGIDs. No supplemental workbook target-table read or native physiological-function claim.

primary_sources.title: Isolated 17,20-lyase deficiency due to the cytochrome b5 mutation W27X.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract supports a human CYB5A stop variant and steroid phenotype. Full original unavailable; the tentative allosteric interpretation is not treated as direct mechanistic measurement.

primary_sources.title: The human liver and reticulocyte cytochrome b5 mRNAs are products from a single gene.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract supports the common gene and alternative transcripts for human reticulocyte and liver products. Full original not recovered; no additional assay scope inferred.

primary_sources.title: Amino acid sequences of cytochrome b5 from human, porcine, and bovine erythrocytes and comparison with liver microsomal cytochrome b5.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract directly describes human erythrocyte protein sequencing and comparison with liver protein. Historical 97-residue mature-chain numbering is distinguished from the current 98-residue translated product. Full original not recovered.

primary_sources.title: Structure of cytochrome b5 and its topology in the microsomal membrane.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract includes human liver protein sequence and rabbit microsomal topology context. The historical C-terminal topology model is not asserted as universally established; full original not recovered.

primary_sources.title: A missense mutation in the human cytochrome b5 gene causes 46,XY disorder of sex development due to true isolated 17,20 lyase deficiency.
primary_sources.assessment: Selected complete original Methods/Results/Discussion were read. Human CYB5A/CYP17A1 coexpression and radiotracer steroid assays directly establish enhancement; H44L heme loss is a structural prediction, not a measurement. The later mechanistic papers preclude an exclusively non-redox interpretation.

primary_sources.title: Evidence that cytochrome b5 acts as a redox donor in CYP17A1 mediated androgen synthesis.
primary_sources.assessment: Selected complete original Methods/Results/Discussion compare iron b5 with redox-inactive Mn-b5 in nanodiscs. Binding without enhancement is distinguished from electron donation. Exact b5 species is delegated to earlier protein protocols in the main text, so no human CYB5A-specific IDA is asserted.

primary_sources.title: Cytochrome b(5) enhances androgen synthesis by rapidly reducing the CYP17A1 oxy-complex in the lyase step.
primary_sources.assessment: Selected complete original Methods/Results directly measure electron transfer using human His-CYP17A1, rat full-length reductase and rabbit b5. This is mechanistic ortholog support, not a human-b5 or soluble-human-product experiment.

primary_sources.title: Substrate-Specific Allosteric Effects on the Enhancement of CYP17A1 Lyase Efficiency by Cytochrome b(5).
primary_sources.assessment: Selected complete original main text establishes substrate-dependent resonance-Raman conformational effects in addition to prior redox evidence. Separate supplementary protocols were not read and exact b5 species/construct is not independently assigned.

primary_sources.title: NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase and cytochrome b5 isoforms as models for the study of post-translational targeting to the endoplasmic reticulum.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete review abstract explicitly distinguishes the separate ER and mitochondrial cytochrome-b5 genes from dual-localized reductase. Full original unavailable; this raises a source/model identity question rather than establishing a universal negative localization.

primary_sources.title: A novel point mutation in a 3' splice site of the NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase gene results in immunologically undetectable enzyme and impaired NADH-dependent ascorbate regeneration in cultured fibroblasts of a patient with type II hereditary methemoglobinemia.
primary_sources.assessment: Complete abstract verifies human reductase deficiency and decreased ascorbate-regeneration activity, but does not settle the specific CYB5A mitochondrial localization. Original scan/XML access attempts failed; no title-based misattribution claim.

provider_access.manual_research: Source-specific original reads, official records and independent bounded consultation; no fabricated provider report.
